If you enjoy RTS games, this is one of the best. It’s challenging early on as you learn to build a stable economy, but mastering it — and interlinking your regions — is deeply satisfying. The economic system is rich and realistic: oversupplying goods crashes prices and the market for them, so careful management is essential. Specialisation, logistics, and resource variety add strategic depth.

Negatives- Development is slow, with infrequent major updates instead of regular small updates. Resident chats can be repetitive, and more music variety alongside additional brief resident conversations would benefit the game. Hopefully, the developer will prioritise adding more policies and development branches, as well as allowing timber to be traded. At the moment, it is possible to become softlocked if you try to rebuild your logging camp and the required materials are redirected elsewhere. In that situation, the only solution is to destroy other buildings to reclaim the timber.

That said, upcoming features like Castle Sieges promise to make an already outstanding RTS game even better.

Got this on sale and seemed like a good deal at the time. I was able to quickly build a successful settlement, then I just kind of ran out of things to do. The trailer and description implies a much deeper, more complex game than what is available.

The bones for a great game are here, but the way this is being presented to the public is deceptive. For the amount of copes sold and the amount of hype around this game, I would consider it a disappointment at this juncture. Not a bad game, just not what we were expecting.

I am hoping that more updates will release more content, but I am skeptical given how incomplete this game is after several years in development. I will happily change my rating if that is the case, but at this point, I would only recommend this game if you find it in the bargain bin.

P.S.: I have so many hours logged because I stepped away from my computer and forgot to come back and shut it down for over 24hr hours. I probably logged 25 hours on the game, so I did give it an honest attempt.

Don't have much to add that hasn't already been posted. Game is aesthetically pleasing and if you like builders, it is satisfying to grow your town as well as experience the ups and downs of trying to figure the optimal build order. For me, things really made sense on my third play through. Once I figured the game out, realized it is a pretty rigid path of how you build and what sequence and where to invest development points. Some development points are so essential that others are just non-viable because by the time you are a large town you are achieving the game goals. I like how global trade is essential. But as other have said, the interaction between different regions you control is almost non-existent and lacking a tangible reason to develop. You are pretty much forced to restart your game to ensure you start in a fertile region.

So I am giving the game a thumbs up based on concept and potential and recommend waiting for it to be on sale prior to giving it a try.

I've played Manor Lords for about 5 hours now and am enjoying it a lot. One thing that especially strikes me about this game is that the dev appears to be responsive to the community. I looked up how to set production limits for different industries and found a year-old Reddit post requesting that the dev add this feature. He did, and this is just one example. On top of this, the game has a lot of detail that adds to the layout of your civilization, and even the layout of individual plots of land. This is a very detailed game that feels pretty polished for an early access title. Oh, and it looks gorgeous!

Manor lords is a unique take on the rts genre and I have been enjoying it thoroughly. The attention to detail in structures , creatures and landscape are just a cherry on top of something that might be one of the best city builders I have seen. It´s medieval setting makes it so that it is not too basic , but has simplicity to it that I personally miss in a lot of city builders. The combat system is also very unique for what is normally a pretty normal to quiet pleasant city builder. As an rts game it doesn´t have that weak combat feeling of something like civilization. Units here feel direct and responsive which I prefer. The only negative I can think about is that it may be a lot for some people because of the micromanagement style this game uses. The more towns you build the more people you have the worry about and that’s not always the most pleasant thing to deal with since every town is another region making it so you can not have a general overview of resources and workforce. But if you can get past through the sometimes rather intense micromanagement , you can see the beauty the game has and hopefully it will have many updates to come.

While the potential of the game is clear, and you can dream of all possibilities, you do not have to wait to get a playable experience. As it stands, the game is a lot of fun, it's beautiful, and offers both city-building, micro-economics, and military readiness. The game can still be improved, though, the largest current issue being collaborating over multiple regions. Sending resources to and from regions is desperately needed to better balance your macro economy on larger maps.

City builder: great early game, then mid game and late game fall off completely. Perks are not implemented, skill tree doesn't work, diplomacy doesn't work, late game systems are not even in the game yet, trading doesn't work or is wonky.

You'll see people glazing this game because "small developer" and the "ceo" actually wrote something in an update note!!! Not mentioning the fact that the update is nothing but a new map and some "optimizations," nothing towards what they promise to actually serve the game in a meaningful way.

It's an interesting game, with some great ideas and concepts not seen in other city building games (being able to walk around your city in 3rd person for one) though i couldn't suggest anyone pay for it in it's current state unless you are wanting to help out the devs by reporting bugs/game play issues. 
It's far from ready, you'll have issues with your towns peoples AI's, and if you are using an ARM GPU, you'll encounter many graphical errors and bugs (roads not rendering, snow fall bugging and making buildings impossible to see to name a few). 
you'll notice all people who have left positive reviews have no more than 50 hours of game play, for a city sim, this is tiny amount of hours, and it's clear why people stop playing after a certain point, it simply is not ready and there a much better options.

Glad i own it though, should be great in a few years, i hope.

Don't expect a Total War game in therms of battle frecuency. It is a city management game, your focus is going to grow your settlement and keep them safe from hunger. But then it integrates that element of battles to add realism to the whole city builder genre, first vs raiders then vs a strong AI that is gonna require you to have a strategy from the start.

And here there is an element that I don't think anyone has pointed out : The area where you start is random and is going to force you to adapt, and if you add to that the development ( and policies ) tree you have an element of old RTS game ( AoE style ) that is what is going to add that replayability.

100% recomended, game still needs content but considering the price tag and that it was made by only one developer I think if you like this type of genre you will enjoy it a lot.
